When is allocative efficiency achieved?

options.A: when a perfectly competitive market is in equilibrium
options.B: when everybody who needs the product can obtain it
options.C: when firms produce at the lowest possible cost
options.D: when monopolistic firms make normal profits

questions.questionText: A consumer spends all of their income on only two goods, X and Y. The consumer is initially in equilibrium, maximising their total utility. The consumer’s tastes change and they get less utility from consuming good Y. The prices of both goods are unchanged. What would be a rational response from the consumer? good X good Y

options.C: buy more unchanged

questions.questionText: When might a moral hazard occur?

options.A: When a consumer does not have full information about a product.
options.B: When a person undertakes an activity that causes harm to another person.
options.C: When a person undertakes a risky activity, knowing another person bears the risk.
options.D: When the seller of a product has more information than the buyer.

questions.questionText: Twomanufacturingfirmsinthesameindustry,producingsimilarproducts,areconsideringmerging together. What would be the least convincing reason for merging?

questions.questionText: The marginal social benefit of consuming a drink is less than the marginal private benefit. What would be the best policy to improve resource allocation in this market?

options.A: give a subsidy to the producers of the drink
options.B: increase competition in the drink industry
options.C: impose a maximum price for the drink above the market equilibrium price
options.D: impose a per unit tax on the drink

questions.questionText: A country’s government banned cigarette smoking in enclosed public spaces, such as offices, shops, bars and restaurants. What is a government failure arising from this ban?

options.A: decreased consumption of cigarettes by smokers
options.B: decreased levels of passive cigarette smoking by non-smokers
options.C: increased litter from used cigarettes outside offices and shops
options.D: increased sales of cigarette substitutes like nicotine patches and gum

questions.questionText: A worker has a low wage. They have little incentive to earn extra income because they will pay more income tax and receive fewer means-tested benefits. What describes this worker’s situation?

options.C: poverty trap

questions.questionText: What is not an outcome of the existence of private property rights?

options.A: They encourage private owners to conserve property when its value is expected to rise.
options.B: They give private owners the incentive to manage their property carefully.
options.C: They make private owners accountable for damage to others from property misuse.
options.D: They prevent private owners gaining from using resources to benefit others.
